goal: Keep recall project and configuration views isolated across shared caches and warm processes
asset: Scoped corpus reads, schema namespaces and authenticated warm recall
scope: Per-section Codex metadata and immutable rollout header scope
Clone-wide worktree project view without unrelated repository mixing
Reader implementation changes isolate schema slots
Warm process keys include default configuration and cache environment
Exact cwd/full-path scope by default and explicit projectScopes for basename labels
outOfScope: Inferring project ownership from arbitrary prose without scope metadata

record.question: What identifies the source policy view cached or served to a recall caller?

options.strongest_objection: Git project views and parser/configuration changes must invalidate the corresponding caches
Aggregated metadata and daemon environment reuse can return another project or configuration corpus

record.rationale: Bind each passage to its own metadata scope, each clone view to its common repository identity and each warm process to all source-configuring environment; namespace reader policy revisions.
evidence: Executed reproduction: raw_memories first unrelated section is indexed under the last section cwd
Focused regression counterexamples cover warm config crossover and worktree exclusion

costs.cost: One Git view discovery per source build and explicit cache keys for source-affecting configuration
evidence: Existing readers and warm cache already collect source metadata and environment keys

costs.cost: Cross-project memory leakage and stale policy cache reuse
evidence: Counterexample raw_memories indexed OTHER_PROJECT_SECRET for report-service

requirements.statement: Unrelated aggregate or rollout sections never enter a project view; basename labels need an explicit mapping to one canonical project; sibling worktrees share canonical project knowledge; reader policy revisions and config roots cannot reuse an incompatible cache or daemon
requirements.counterexample: The last cwd scopes all sections, an XDG_CONFIG_HOME change returns the prior daemon corpus, or a sibling worktree loses canonical repo knowledge

checks.scope: Actual parser, Git sibling worktree, alternate reader installation and warm hook with two configurations
assumptions: Explicit allowUnscoped and configured peer path aliases remain user-controlled corpus policy

challenges.claim: Can shared caches use one key for every checkout of the same clone?
challenges.resolution: Only when corpus configuration and canonical project scope agree; unrelated repositories retain distinct scope identities and source readers apply the full project view.

challenges.claim: Does a Project:frontend heading uniquely identify a repository?
challenges.resolution: No. Exact cwd/full-path scope is required by default. A configured projectScopes label maps to one absolute local project root and its sibling worktrees; unrelated repositories with the same basename are excluded.
